info.title: Google Ads Service
info.description: Wraps the Google Ads API (v23) for MCC agency management. Handles OAuth, account linking, campaign CRUD, and performance reporting.

mailbox.description: The connected Google account holding the thread

fromAddress.description: The owner address a reply is written from: the address the person wrote to, or that answered them, on the newest message where one took part

lastMessageAt.description: When the thread's newest message was sent (any participant)

sendPermission.description: The mailbox's Google grant includes gmail.send. False = a reply is refused with google_send_permission_missing until the org owner reconnects Google

to.description: The person: must take part in the thread

threadId.description: Gmail thread id, as served by GET /orgs/google/threads/latest

bodyText.description: Plain-text part; derived from bodyHtml when absent

leadId.description: The person's lead id in lead-service (the same `leadId` the broadcast send carries). The reply is then declared to runs-service's ledger as a `message_sent` of that lead on this request's run (consuming its `message_written` and `email_checked`), dated when Gmail accepted it. Absent = the email still leaves, but its message_sent stays undeclared (never declared under a guessed subject).

inReplyTo.description: Message-ID of the thread's newest message (In-Reply-To; also appended to References)

recorded.description: The sent message was written to the mirror (false = logged; the 15-min delta picks it up)

disconnectError.description: Why the last disconnect attempt failed (the mailbox is still connected; retry the disconnect). Null when none failed.
Why the last disconnect attempt failed (the mailbox is still connected; retry the disconnect). Null when none failed.

get.summary: List connected Google accounts for the org
get.description: Returns the set of Google (Gmail) accounts the org has connected via OAuth. Sourced from google_oauth_tokens, scoped by x-org-id.

delete.description: Revokes the grant at Google (refresh token, bounded wait), then marks the account disconnected in one row update and answers: from then on it is not listed by GET /orgs/google/accounts, never synced again, and every mirror write for it is refused. Everything mirrored for it (Gmail messages + contacts, bronze and silver) is deleted in the background in batches (mirror=deleting), resumed after a restart. A Google revoke failure answers 502 reason=google_revoke_failed and leaves the connection intact (listed with disconnectError) so the call can be retried. An already-revoked grant (the user removed the app at Google) is reported as grant=already_revoked; disconnecting an account already disconnecting answers 200 the same way. Contact links (CRM tagging) are org state and are kept. Reconnecting the same address later starts a fresh mirror.

parameters.name: email
parameters.description: The connected Google account email (URL-encoded). Matched case-insensitively.

404.description: This org has no connected account with that email (reason=account_not_found)

502.description: Google did not confirm the revoke (reason=google_revoke_failed). The account stays connected; retry.

post.summary: Start a Google connection (mailbox by default, or calendar)
post.description: Generates a Google authorize URL with PKCE and persists state + verifier in google_oauth_pending (10 minute TTL). connection=mailbox (default) asks Gmail read + send and Contacts read; connection=calendar asks, on its own consent, Calendar events read + Google Meet read (attendance). The same /auth/callback finishes both and answers which connection it stored.

get.summary: Google CRM OAuth callback (Gmail + People readonly)
get.description: Exchanges code+PKCE for tokens, stores refresh token in google_oauth_tokens (one row per (org_id, google_account_email)), then starts an async sync of the org's mailboxes so the new one mirrors with no further step. The response carries syncJobId; poll GET /orgs/google/sync/{jobId}.

post.summary: Start an async Gmail + People sync for all connected Google accounts of the org
post.description: Backfill (last GOOGLE_GMAIL_BACKFILL_DAYS for Gmail; full People connections) on first sync, delta thereafter using Gmail historyId and People syncToken. Idempotent: re-runs produce no duplicate rows. Returns 202 immediately with a jobId; the caller must poll GET /orgs/google/sync/{jobId} until status != 'running'.

get.summary: Get the status of an async sync job
get.description: Returns the current status (running | succeeded | failed) of a sync job. On success, summary is populated; on failure, error contains the error message. Lookup is org-scoped: jobs from other orgs return 404.

404.description: Sync job not found for this org

get.summary: List raw Gmail messages (bronze) for the org

parameters.name: participant
parameters.description: Filter to one contact's email thread: only messages where this email appears as a From/To/Cc participant. Ordered by the message's own email date (newest first).

get.summary: Read the whole exchange with one person out of the Gmail mirror
get.description: Every message exchanged with the given address, both directions, grouped by thread and ordered oldest first, with readable bodies derived from the stored Gmail payload. Without fresh it is a read that never calls Google. With fresh=true the org's connected Gmail mailboxes are first brought up to date (one Gmail history delta per mailbox, the same pass the 15-minute refresh runs; concurrent fresh reads of one org share one refresh, and a refresh started more than 5 seconds before the read is never reused), so mail sent or received seconds ago is in the answer; when that refresh fails (or a mailbox has not finished its first sync) the answer is 502 with reason gmail_refresh_failed or gmail_mirror_not_caught_up, never the stale mirror. Org-scoped in the query itself. Three answers stay distinct: 404 reason=no_google_account_connected (no mailbox connected), 404 reason=no_messages (nobody has this exchange), and 200 with status=unreadable|partial (we hold it and could not read it). Inside a 200, a message with bodyStatus="empty" genuinely says nothing, while bodyStatus="unavailable" means its text is not readable from the stored payload. bodyText is what the sender actually wrote: quoted history, signature, footers, unsubscribe blocks and long tracking URLs removed; lines are kept or dropped verbatim, never rewritten. The full original stays in bodyTextOriginal. Reply separators, quote markers, the signature delimiter and long URLs are removed structurally; every remaining line is classified by a Jev judgment (chat-service, input tokens billed to the calling org on this run), persisted per message so a message is judged once, never per read. bodyCleanStatus says how bodyText was derived: cleaned (judged), nothing_kept (nothing was the sender's words: bodyText is the ORIGINAL, never an empty message), pending (over this read's judging budget of 30 messages, newest judged first: structural clean only, judged on a later read), judge_failed (structural clean only, retried next read), not_applicable (no readable body).

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum messages returned (default 200). When exceeded the most RECENT messages are kept and truncated=true.

parameters.name: fresh
parameters.description: true: bring the org's Gmail mirror up to date before reading (mail sent seconds ago is included). A failed refresh answers 502, never the stale mirror.

200.description: The exchange with this address, grouped by thread, oldest first

404.description: No mailbox connected for this org, or no exchange with this address

502.description: fresh=true and the Gmail mirror could not be brought up to date (reason gmail_refresh_failed or gmail_mirror_not_caught_up). Never answered with the stale mirror.

get.summary: List who the org's connected mailbox has been in conversation with
get.description: Every counterpart address the connected Gmail mailbox(es) have exchanged mail with, read out of the mirror (never calls Google). "In conversation" means the mailbox owner WROTE to them: the address appears in To or Cc of a message sent from an owner address. Pure inbound senders the owner never wrote to (newsletters, notifications) are excluded. Owner addresses (returned as ownerAddresses) = the org's connected Google account emails plus every sender of a SENT-labelled message (send-as aliases). Per address: outboundMessages = messages sent from an owner address with this address in To/Cc (counted once per message); inboundMessages = messages whose From is this address; first/last activity over those messages. Every listed address matches GET /orgs/google/conversation?email=<address> (same lower-cased From/To/Cc matching), so it opens to a non-empty conversation there. Sorted by lastMessageAt desc, then email asc (total order, stable across pages). total is the full count across all pages; twoWayTotal counts those with at least one inbound message. 404 reason=no_google_account_connected means no mailbox is connected; a connected mailbox with nobody answers 200 with total=0.

200.description: The correspondents page, with totals across all pages

404.description: No Google account is connected for this org

get.summary: Read the exchange between one person and our staff, out of the staff Gmail mirrors
get.description: Internal, service-to-service. Reads only mailboxes whose Google account is a staff address, across every org that mirrors one, and returns only the messages BETWEEN a staff address and the given person (staff -> person with the person in To/Cc, or person -> staff with a staff address in To/Cc). Never the rest of a thread, never any other message of the mailbox. Same response shape as /orgs/google/conversation; direction is always inbound or outbound. Bodies are NOT cleaned here: bodyText equals bodyTextOriginal and bodyCleanStatus is not_cleaned. 404 reason=no_staff_mailbox_connected (no staff mailbox mirrored) and 404 reason=no_messages (no such exchange) are documented answers.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum messages returned (default 200). When exceeded the most RECENT messages are kept and truncated=true.

200.description: The staff exchange with this address, grouped by thread, oldest first

404.description: No staff mailbox mirrored, or no staff exchange with this address

get.summary: List the org's connected Google Calendars
get.description: Each Google Calendar this org connected (POST /orgs/google/auth/start with connection=calendar, its own consent, never bundled with Gmail) and its health: status=sync_failing when the last read failed (lastSyncError says why, e.g. the grant was removed at Google: reconnect); attendance=meet when Google Meet participant lists can be read, meet_permission_missing when that permission was not granted (attendance stays unknown). Calendars are read every ~15 min.

delete.description: Stops reading the calendar and deletes every event mirrored from it. The Google grant is revoked, EXCEPT when the same Google account is also connected as a mailbox (grant=kept_for_mailbox): a revoke would cut the mailbox too. A Google revoke failure answers 502 reason=google_revoke_failed and keeps the calendar connected (retry). 404 reason=calendar_not_found.

parameters.name: email
parameters.description: The connected calendar's Google account email (URL-encoded). Matched case-insensitively.

404.description: No such calendar connected for this org (reason=calendar_not_found)

502.description: Google did not confirm the revoke (reason=google_revoke_failed). Still connected; retry.

get.summary: Changes feed of Google Calendar events across every org (booked meetings + Meet attendance)
get.description: Internal, service-to-service. Every event of every connected Google Calendar (primary calendar, window 30 days back to 180 days ahead) whose served fields changed after the cursor, oldest change first: a new booking, a reschedule, a cancellation (status=cancelled), or Meet attendance read. An event that changes again comes back again. Each event carries orgId, the calendar's Google account, Google's own status, title, start/end, bookedAt (when the event was created at Google), organizer, attendees (email lower-cased, displayName, responseStatus, organizer, self) and meet: status not_meet (not a Google Meet call: attendance unknown), pending (not ended, or ended and no Meet record yet), record_found (participants = who joined, displayName + kind signed_in|anonymous|phone + joinedAt/leftAt; Meet gives no email), no_record (no Meet record 24h after the end: unknown, NOT 'nobody came'), unavailable (Google refused the Meet read, error says why). Which attendee or participant is which lead is the consumer's judgment: people book from another address. Paging: keep nextCursor and send it back; hasMore=true means ask again now, false means wait for the next poll (calendars are read every ~15 min). No cursor = from the beginning. 400 on a bad cursor.

post.summary: Read staff-mirrored mail sent TO or FROM our own sending mailboxes
post.description: Internal, service-to-service (not proxied to customers). Reads only mailboxes whose Google account is a staff address, across every org that mirrors one, and returns only messages whose To/Cc contains one of the requested addresses (or an address at a requested domain) - direction=inbound - or whose From is one of them - direction=outbound (staff answering via send-as). Built to recover prospect replies that a mailbox-level forward drained into staff Gmail. Each message carries its RFC 5322 Message-ID / In-Reply-To / References (verbatim, angle brackets kept), automation headers (Auto-Submitted, Precedence, X-Autoreply, ...), the top MIME type (multipart/report = delivery report), sender, To, Cc, subject, date and the plain-text body derived from the stored payload (original, not cleaned; no LLM). Paging: keyset on an opaque cursor; send back nextCursor with the same filter until it is null. Order is stable but not chronological. `id` (= mailbox:gmailMessageId) is stable across re-reads. A staff address, or a staff mailbox domain, is refused as a filter (400). since is inclusive, until exclusive, both on sentAt. 404 reason=no_staff_mailbox_connected is a documented answer.

200.description: One page of matching messages; nextCursor null on the last page

400.description: Invalid filter (none given, staff address/domain, bad cursor)

post.summary: Read this org's connected Gmail for mail exchanged with given people
post.description: Org-scoped (the org from x-org-id; only this org's own connected Google mailboxes). Returns every mirrored message whose From is one of the requested addresses (direction=inbound), or that has one of them in To/Cc: sent from one of the org's own addresses (direction=outbound) or by a third party (direction=other). Same per-message fields as /internal/staff-mailboxes/addressed-messages (RFC 5322 Message-ID / In-Reply-To / References verbatim, automation headers, top MIME type, from/to/cc, subject, sentAt, labels, plain-text body from the stored payload, not cleaned, no LLM), plus matchedAddresses (requested addresses found in From/To/Cc). ownerAddresses = the org's own addresses (connected accounts + send-as aliases); a requested address that is one of them is dropped and listed in ignoredAddresses (it would be the whole mailbox). Paging: keyset on an opaque cursor; send back nextCursor with the same body until it is null. Order is stable, not chronological. since is inclusive, until exclusive, both on sentAt. Never calls Google. 404 reason=no_google_account_connected is a documented answer.

200.description: One page of matching messages; nextCursor null on the last page

400.description: Invalid body (no address, more than 1000, bad cursor)

404.description: This org has connected no Google account

get.summary: The Gmail thread holding a person's latest exchange with this org's connected mailboxes
get.description: Org-scoped read of the mirror, never calls Google. Among the threads the person appears in (From/To/Cc; drafts, spam and trash excluded), the one whose newest message is newest, provided an owner address of its mailbox took part (the account email or one of its send-as aliases seen on SENT mail). fromAddress = the address a reply is written from. lastMessageAt lets a caller compare with another transport's latest exchange. sendPermission says whether the grant includes gmail.send. 404 reason=no_google_account_connected | no_messages are documented answers.

404.description: No connected mailbox, or no answerable thread with this person

post.summary: Reply in a Gmail thread from the address the person wrote to
post.description: Sends ONE email in the given Gmail thread through the connected mailbox that holds it, From the thread's owner address (same resolution as GET /orgs/google/threads/latest; it must be one of the mailbox's Gmail send-as addresses), To the person, Subject `Re: <thread subject>`, In-Reply-To = the newest message's Message-ID, References = its References + that id. The sent message is then written to the mirror. Uses the account's own OAuth grant: no metered platform cost. Refusals (nothing sent) carry a `code`: 404 no_google_account_connected | thread_not_found, 403 google_send_permission_missing (the grant lacks gmail.send: the org owner must reconnect Google and grant send access), 422 from_address_not_send_as. Not idempotent: the caller dedupes.

get.summary: List raw Google contacts (bronze) for the org

put.summary: Upsert per-contact CRM links (org/brand/feature tags + reserved status)
put.description: Persists platform org/brand/feature links (and a reserved status) for one Google contact. resourceName is carried in the body, never the path, because Google resourceNames contain "/". Upserts on (org, resourceName).

post.summary: Batch search — multiple queries in one call
post.description: Performs multiple web and/or news searches in parallel and returns all results.
